title: The Distant Inheritance
intro: An email from a lawyer abroad says a stranger left you a huge inheritance.
Tap anything that looks odd to sniff it closer. Pin what is suspicious, clear what is harmless.
When you are sure, decide what to do.

addr.label: A free-mail address
addr.lens: A real law firm writes from its own domain.
addr.why: Look at the address behind the name.

stranger.label: A stranger left you money
stranger.lens: A man you have never met.
stranger.why: Money from strangers does not exist.

amount.label: A huge sum
amount.why: A huge windfall out of nowhere is the bait.

id.label: Asks for your ID and bank details
id.lens: These are used to steal your identity.
id.why: Never send these to a stranger.

fee.label: A fee to release the money
fee.why: A fee to receive a windfall is the scam.

from.label: A barrister's name
from.why: Names and titles are easy to invent.

trap.title: Legal Chambers · Release funds
trap.ask: Upload your ID and pay $1,200 to release $4,500,000.

block_report.line: Reported and deleted. The fake address was blocked.

verify.line: A search showed the same "inheritance" email in many scam warnings. Case cracked.

ignore.line: You stayed safe. But the same scam is still landing on other people.

go_ahead.line: The fee was lost and your ID was used to open accounts in your name. No inheritance ever came.

what_if.go_ahead: A stranger leaving you millions, and a fee to receive it, is the oldest trick there is.
what_if.ignore: Reporting takes two taps and helps protect other people.
what_if.verify: Checking was smart. Reporting it as well helps protect other people.

golden_rule: Money from a stranger that needs a fee to arrive is not an inheritance. Delete it.

quick_check.q: An email says a stranger left you $4,500,000 and you must pay a fee to release it. What do you do?
